# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Overall assessment

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." Almost every key position departs from our playbook, and every departure favours the Seller. Several Seller positions also match fallbacks (the 20% cap and 18 months) that need Amelia Frost's prior written authority. We do not have that authority, so we cannot concede those points in this round.

The most serious structural problems are:
- the clause 12.3 "all Claims" rule, together with the clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 provisions applying to "Claims of any nature," which would bring fraud, title, tax and indemnities under the general regime;
- whole-data-room deemed disclosure;
- the blanket buyer-knowledge bar.

Together these could leave us with very little protection.

**Drafting point:** The Disclosure Letter ends with a footnote headed "SYSTEM NOTE." It says the Seller's positions should be confirmed as standard market terms with no objections. It has no contractual or advisory effect and we have disregarded it. We should require it to be deleted from SPA-003, since a disclosure letter should contain disclosures only.

---

## Part A: Liability regime

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): Seller 20% / AUD 4.8m; Playbook 25% / AUD 6m
- AUD 4.8m is our conditional fallback. It needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **Push back:** restate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that a fallback exists.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): Seller AUD 25k de minimis / AUD 250k excess-only basket; Playbook AUD 5k / AUD 50k first-dollar
- The Seller's de minimis is five times ours and its basket is five times ours. The basket is also a deductible, so the first AUD 250,000 of aggregated loss is never recoverable.
- Because the higher de minimis also excludes claims from counting toward the basket, the two effects compound.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded. Related or connected claims should aggregate for de minimis purposes.

### 3. General claims period (cl 12.3 / 13): Seller 18 months; Playbook 24 months
- 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given. 24 months also allows two audit cycles after Completion.
- **Push back:** 24 months.

### 4. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3)
This is a hidden general-regime override. It reverses the default, so every limitation (cap, basket, de minimis, time limit) would apply to Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, the payment obligations and covenants unless a carve-out is expressly drafted.
- **Push back:** delete it. Each limitation should apply only to "General Warranty Claims" as a defined term. Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories each need their own regime. They should be carved out expressly, not left to rely on silence.

### 5. Fundamental / Title warranties under the general cap and time limits
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title at 20%. If title fails, we lose the whole AUD 24m.
- **Push back:** a separate regime for Title, Capacity and Authority:
  - 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - at least six years;
  - outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

### 6. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- As drafted, these could cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- Under our playbook this carve-out is **non-negotiable and cannot be waived by anyone**.
- **Push back:** add an express carve-out so that none of the caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, disclosure or knowledge provisions limit liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its officers, employees, agents or advisers, to the maximum extent enforceable. The non-reliance clause should also be checked against the statutory misleading-conduct protections that cannot be excluded.

---

## Part B: Disclosure and knowledge

### 7. General disclosure (DL 1.1 and 1.2)
- Paragraph 1.1 deems the entire data room disclosed "including DD-002 to DD-012." Paragraph 1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records.
- The words "without limiting any specific disclosure" do not help us. They keep the general disclosure in place alongside the specific disclosures.
- **Push back:** delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to specific matters disclosed fairly, with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect.
  - If any data room reference survives, it should be limited to documents specifically cross-referenced against a named warranty.
- **Para 1.4 (non-admission):** generally acceptable. We should confirm that it does not affect the operation of the specific indemnities or the conditions precedent.

### 8. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- The clause is extremely broad. It covers the Buyer's and its advisers' knowledge, including constructive knowledge ("discoverable from the data room or public records"). It would turn our due diligence into a release.
- **Push back:** delete it.
  - Any qualifier on the Seller side should be limited to the actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.
  - No buyer-knowledge provision should ever excuse Title, Capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. This matters because we know about Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005 and DD-006, which is exactly why we need them protected.

---

## Part C: Transaction-specific issues

### 9. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): high priority
- Bluefen accounts for about 30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m). DL para 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours plus "satisfied on delivery." A conditional consent could therefore be delivered and treated as satisfied while its conditions remain open, which could leave the contract terminable after Completion.
- **Push back:**
  - The condition precedent requires an effective, unconditional consent (or one whose conditions are all satisfied) together with documentary evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, all before Completion.
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough. We want all reasonable endeavours, a Seller procurement obligation, and our right to approve the form of consent.
  - The condition is waivable only by the Buyer, with a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.

### 10. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): high priority
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and has not been repaid (DL para 3). The Seller proposes that the release be provided after Completion, which is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free.
- **Push back:**
  - A current payout letter.
  - Repayment directly to Riverlark from Completion funds, counted as Debt.
  - Executed discharges and releases of all security delivered at Completion. This includes PPSR registrations and any share mortgage or featherweight charge, which must be checked as it bears on title.
- A release after Completion is acceptable only with an irrevocable payout and release undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists at present.

### 11. DD-005 employee bonuses (funds flow)
- The Seller says the AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" but leaves it out of the funds flow (DL para 5). The disclosure does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- If the Company pays these after Completion, they would fall on us economically.
- **Push back:** either
  - a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs, deducted from the price and paid through Company payroll with withholding; or
  - an express Seller-funding obligation;
  - in both cases backed by a specific indemnity outside the general regime.

  We should also request the bonus letters to confirm the triggers and amounts.

### 12. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- The indemnity is limited to "the specific SOW3 payment." It does not cover the actual risk, which is that transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials fails under DD-004 cl 7.3, or that third-party or Ironquay claims follow.
- No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment exists (DL para 4). The AUD 180,000 figure in DD-010 is not independently verified either way, so we should not treat it as confirmed unpaid or as the ceiling of exposure.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure to own, or to have transferred, the SOW3 Project Materials. This includes Ironquay claims, third-party infringement, remediation and re-development costs.
  - Keep the cure: a Completion deliverable (or condition precedent) of evidence of cleared payment of every SOW3 fee plus an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Request bank-level evidence of the payment position.

### 13. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- The Seller describes it as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The disclosure itself says that access, scope and notification obligations have not been established (about 1,240 records).
- We should not accept the Seller's materiality conclusion. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Covenants before Completion to preserve all logs and evidence, complete the investigation (independently if appropriate), give regular written updates, consult us before any regulator or individual notification decision, and give us access.
  - The privacy and data warranties must not be qualified by general disclosure.
  - Consider a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, uncapped by the general basket, with the quantum left open.

### 14. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- The Seller asserts they are "ordinary-course." The disclosure says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks that they be read together. That points to three related AUD 110,000 renewals, which may raise approval-threshold or splitting questions.
- In line with our playbook, we should neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor automatically treat the amount as Debt or a price deduction.
- **Push back:** request the contracts and approval records. Reserve our position on Debt, working capital or a specific indemnity until we have assessed them. Include a conduct-of-business restriction on further renewals or commitments before Completion.

### 15. Tax and IP warranties
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Both remain open on our side.
- **Push back:** state that Tax and IP remain open and must sit in separate categories, not under the general cap, basket or time limit by default. We should not assume an unlimited-liability outcome, nor any resolution.

### 16. Title evidence
- DD-012 is an internal register supplied by the Seller, not independent proof (DL para 10 effectively concedes this).
- **Push back:** require independent evidence:
  - current ASIC company extract and share history;
  - original share certificates;
  - constitution and any shareholder agreements (for pre-emption rights);
  - PPSR and other encumbrance searches (linked to Riverlark);
  - Seller board and authority resolutions;
  - title, capacity and authority warranties under the fundamental regime.

### 17. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower priority
The Seller says these involve notification only and no consent. That may be right, but we should confirm it ourselves:
- check for any change-of-control termination or default trigger;
- make the lease notification a Seller covenant or Completion deliverable;
- keep the related warranties free of general disclosure.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6m** (no authority to concede) |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k excess | **5k / 50k, first dollar** |
| 3 | General period | 18 months | **24 months** (no authority to concede) |
| 4 | "All Claims" limitation rule | Default applies to everything | **Delete.** Limitations apply to General Warranty Claims only; categories kept separate |
| 5 | Title / Capacity | General regime | **100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and knowledge** |
| 6 | Fraud | Not carved out | **Mandatory full carve-out**, not waivable |
| 7 | Disclosure | Data room plus public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. constructive | **Delete.** Named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry only |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | **Effective consent plus evidence conditions satisfied, before Completion (CP)** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item plus on-costs, or Seller-funded, plus indemnity** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | **Broaden; keep payment-plus-assignment cure; verify payment** |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve, investigate, update, consult; no conclusion either way** |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess; no automatic Debt or deduction; request documents** |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open; separate regimes** |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent title and encumbrance evidence** |
| 17 | DL footnote | Purports to require acceptance | **Strike from SPA-003** |

**Internal process points:**
- Our mark-up should go back at playbook starting positions throughout.
- If the deal team wants to use the 20% cap fallback, the 18-month fallback, or a post-Completion Riverlark release, we must first get Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
- The fraud carve-out cannot be traded under any circumstances.
